description: Hand-labeled pilot set for evaluating trust propagation over the compiler's own corpus. Every claim is a real, verbatim quote from a file under data/raw/ (source_path is relative to data/raw/) — nothing here is synthetic text invented for the dataset, though the underlying corpus itself is the repo's fictional Aurora Labs / TeaBuddy sample domain. See documentation/21-trust-eval-dataset.md for labeling protocol and known limitations.

gold_labels.correct: Current, authoritative value for this claim group.
gold_labels.incorrect: Actively wrong; not just outdated, factually false when it was written.
gold_labels.superseded: Was true/asserted at the time, later corrected or replaced by a newer source.
gold_labels.scope_dependent: Not a contradiction — different values are each valid under different conditions (node count, deployment stage, etc.).
gold_labels.disputed: Still asserted by some sources, but undermined by a documented dependency on another claim this dataset marks incorrect/superseded.

claim_groups.subject: Nova Widget default sensor read interval
claim_groups.description: How often a Nova Widget takes a reading by default. Kickoff notes said hourly; every source from the May 15 spec onward says 15 minutes and explicitly calls the hourly figure a mistake.

claims.quote: Power target | 2 years on CR2032 with hourly readings
claims.note: Earliest source; superseded two weeks later by the spec.

claims.quote: Default: every 15 minutes when mesh is active. [...] Note: kickoff notes mentioned hourly default; this spec changes to 15 min for beta feedback.
claims.note: First source to state 15 min and explicitly flag the kickoff figure as changed.

claims.quote: Default read interval: 15 minutes (ignore old PDF saying hourly).
claims.note: Corroborates nri-2; explicitly disclaims the old (hourly) figure.

claims.quote: Depends on node count and read interval (15 min default).
claims.note: Corroborates nri-2.

claims.quote: Default read interval remains 15 minutes (NOT hourly — kickoff slides were wrong)
claims.note: Explicitly contradicts nri-1 by name ("kickoff slides").

claims.quote: Read interval: 15 min (spec authoritative)
claims.note: Corroborates nri-2, cites the spec as the authority.

claims.quote: 15 minutes. Some older docs say hourly — that was a kickoff mistake.
claims.note: Corroborates nri-2; names the kickoff notes as the origin of the error.

claims.quote: Read interval is set to 15 minutes per the current firmware default (0.3.8), so this isn't an interval misconfiguration.
claims.note: Corroborates nri-2 from an independent (email) channel.

claim_groups.subject: Nova Widget battery cell type
claim_groups.description: CR2032 is the correct cell. An early version of a competitor's teardown blog said CR2450; the blog post itself was later corrected in place, and the error is independently reported in a team transcript and the customer FAQ.

claims.quote: Power target | 2 years on CR2032 with hourly readings
claims.note: Correct on cell type even though this same source is wrong on read interval (see nova_read_interval) — a reminder that trust should be scored per-claim, not per-source.

claims.quote: Battery: CR2032 primary cell
claims.note: Corroborates nbc-1.

claims.quote: An earlier version of this post said Nova used a CR2450 battery. That was wrong — the beta unit uses CR2032. Apologies to Aurora Labs.
claims.note: Self-correcting source: the file's current text documents its own prior error inline, dated one day after the original post.

claims.value: CR2450 was wrong; CR2032 is correct
claims.quote: Alex's blog had the wrong battery. CR2450. We use two-oh-three-two.
claims.note: Independent (spoken/transcript) confirmation that CR2450 was an error and CR2032 is correct.

claims.quote: CR2032 nominal 220mAh (not 240 — datasheet variance)
claims.note: Corroborates nbc-1/nbc-2.

claims.value: CR2032; CR2450 explicitly flagged as wrong
claims.quote: CR2032. Some blog posts incorrectly said CR2450 — corrected in wiki.
claims.note: Corroborates nbc-1/nbc-2 and explicitly names the CR2450 error (matches nbc-3).

claim_groups.subject: Nova Widget battery life claim (marketing vs. engineering)
claim_groups.description: Not a simple true/false pair: marketing's 24-month figure and engineering's 18-month figure describe different deployment sizes. But the power-budget notes reveal the marketing figure additionally rests on the debunked hourly read interval, which moves it from merely scope-dependent to disputed.

claims.quote: Marketing target: 24 months at 15-minute intervals in moderate mesh (≤ 5 nodes).
claims.note: As stated here, scoped to <=5 nodes at 15-min intervals — internally consistent.

claims.quote: Internal engineering target: 18 months minimum at 10 nodes — do not publish externally.
claims.note: Stress-case internal figure; treated as the authoritative number for the worst-case deployment.

claims.value: engineering 18mo @ 10 nodes; marketing may still say 2yr
claims.quote: Battery life: engineering 18mo @ 10 nodes; marketing may still say 2yr
claims.note: Corroborates nbl-1/nbl-2 and flags the marketing/engineering divergence as still unresolved as of this release.

claims.quote: Total ~0.19 mAh/day → ~18 months (engineering claim)
claims.note: Corroborates nbl-2 with a bottom-up power calculation.

claims.value: 2 years (marketing, relies on wrong read interval)
claims.quote: Marketing slide "2 years" assumes 6 nodes + optimistic cell + hourly reads (WRONG interval)
claims.note: Downgraded from scope_dependent to disputed: this source shows the marketing figure's inputs include the hourly read interval, which nova_read_interval's gold labels mark superseded/incorrect. A propagation algorithm that only looks within this claim group cannot see that dependency — flagged as a known limitation in the methodology doc.

claim_groups.subject: TeaBuddy herbal steep preset timing constant
claim_groups.description: A single changelog entry documents its own contradiction: the firmware constant (7:00) was aligned to fix a mismatch with marketing copy (5:00). Only one raw source currently documents this, so both claims share it — a candidate for follow-up ingestion (e.g. the marketing copy itself) in a future dataset version.

claims.quote: Herbal preset constant aligned to 7:00 (was 5:00 in marketing copy — CONTRADICTION fixed in firmware only)
claims.note: The 5:00 value as it existed in marketing copy prior to this fix; not independently sourced yet.

claims.quote: Herbal preset constant aligned to 7:00 (was 5:00 in marketing copy — CONTRADICTION fixed in firmware only)
claims.note: Current firmware value as of the v0.9.4 changelog entry; the source itself notes the fix has not propagated back to marketing copy.

claim_groups.subject: MeshSync relay-mode battery drain root cause (MESH-118)
claim_groups.description: A clean, undisputed corroboration chain across three emails: a field report, an engineering confirmation with root cause, and a beta announcement of the fix. Included as a contrast case with no contradictions, so a propagation algorithm is checked against over-penalizing agreement as much as it is checked against under-penalizing disputes.

claims.value: Relay mode drains battery ~30% faster than spec; suspected cause: relay radio not sleeping between hops
claims.quote: Batch 4 field units are reporting battery drain roughly 30% faster than spec once MeshSync relay mode is enabled. [...] Suspect the relay radio is staying awake between hops instead of sleeping. Filed as MESH-118.
claims.note: Initial field report; hypothesis, later confirmed.

claims.value: Confirmed: sleep timer resets on every received packet; fix reduces radio wake time 400ms -> 80ms per hop
claims.quote: Confirmed on the bench. The relay radio's sleep timer resets on every received packet, so a busy mesh never lets it sleep. Draft fix in MESH-118 drops radio wake time from 400ms to 80ms per hop.
claims.note: Independent engineering confirmation of mrd-1's hypothesis with root cause and a concrete fix.

claims.quote: 0.3.9 is up for the batch 4 retest — this build addresses the MeshSync relay battery drain reported earlier this week (MESH-118).
claims.note: Corroborates mrd-1/mrd-2 by referencing the same ticket and rolling the fix into a beta build.

claim_groups.subject: Nova Widget enclosure IP rating (beta vs. GA)
claim_groups.description: Every source agrees on the same status: IP54 for beta units, with an IP65 tooled variant planned but blocked on a ~$8k gasket tooling cost, later confirmed deferred. Included as a strongly-corroborating (non-contradictory) claim group to balance the dataset, which otherwise skews toward disputed/superseded cases — this tests that propagation does not manufacture disagreement where sources actually agree, and gives the graph more genuine corroborates edges to propagate over.

claims.value: IP54 beta; IP65 planned for GA (~$8k gasket tooling)
claims.quote: IP54 for beta units. IP65 planned for GA if gasket tooling budget allows (~$8k).
claims.note: Earliest source; establishes the baseline status other sources corroborate.

claims.value: IP54 beta; IP65 pending the $8k tool
claims.quote: IP54 is fine for beta; IP65 needs the $8k tool Mira mentioned in the spec.
claims.note: Jonah corroborates the spec draft two weeks later.

claims.value: IP54 ok; IP65 blocked on the $8k tool
claims.quote: IP54 ok. IP65 = $8k tool rip
claims.note: Informal standup note, same status as nip-1/nip-2.

claims.quote: IP65 tooled variant deferred ($7,850 quote)
claims.note: A more precise tooling quote ($7,850) refining the earlier ~$8k estimate, not a conflicting figure — corroborates rather than contradicts.

claims.value: IP54 beta shipping; IP65 tooling ($8k) deferred
claims.quote: IP65 tooling $8k deferred; shipping IP54 beta with clear splash-resistance language
claims.note: Latest source; confirms the deferred status as of the investor update.
